txt: The a control or special token SHALL be minted only from the specials-parsing path such as EncodeSpecial, never from untrusted text passed through plain Encode.
The a new tokenizer or segmentation path SHALL close both the marker-matching pre-split and the segmentation search itself, and prove the gate by mutation testing that an always-parse design fails.

The a model architecture's per-block features such as biases, QK-norm and the Granite scalars SHALL be applied in one block stack that DecodeStep, StreamStep and SelfExtendForward all route through, with attention as the only pluggable part.
IF a duplicated decode path must remain, THEN the package SHALL name it in godoc and pin it with a cross-path test comparing tokens, using nonzero feature values plus a feature-free control.

note:
Implemented and validated. keepSinkRecent now copies the two retained regions as typed row blocks instead of per-element AtF64/SetF64.

MEASURED 6,099,284 -> 147,826 ns on BenchmarkKeepSinkRecent (2048x2048 -> 516x2048, F32), 41x, throughput 693 -> 28,595 MB/s. Interleaved three-round file-copy toggle, one host, one session, medians. The benchmark is NEW — the package streaming tests use sinks=2 and window=6, far too small to reach the bound, so nothing had ever measured this path.

THE RESULT WAS DISTRUSTED AND CHECKED. 41x against a predicted 5-8x is the shape of a benchmark measuring nothing (elided work or an early return), so both arms allocation profiles were compared: 4,227,3xx B/op each, identical work and identical output size. The prediction was low because it came from a per-element-versus-row-copy micro ratio; at roughly 1M elements the per-element path additionally thrashes cache while the typed copy is bandwidth-bound.

BIT-IDENTITY: exact. A same-dtype copy moves the same bits, and the SetF64(AtF64(...)) it replaces was already an exact round trip. TestKeepSinkRecentMatchesPerElement pins it element-for-element against the per-element reference across F32 and F64 and six geometries — past the bound, at the bound, below it, degenerate widths, no sinks, no window — and is PROVEN NON-VACUOUS by mutation: swapping the window source offset turns it red, restoring turns it green.

REFACTOR NOTE: copyRows gained a copyRowsFrom sibling taking a source offset, which the original now delegates to. It returns false for dtypes it cannot move verbatim, so keepSinkRecent keeps its generic per-element fallback for those — the typed path covers F32, F64, F16 and BF16 only, whereas the code it replaced handled any dtype.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the second half of the original finding — replacing the concatRows call at streaming.go:86-87 with a ring-buffer append so the bounded cache stops being reallocated per layer per token. That is the same defect class as the rowBuf propagation task and belongs with it, not here. No perfscan rule was minted: this is the same per-element-copy shape the PS4004 detector already covers, and the site is exactly what a widened PS1001 would flag — both are tracked in their own tasks.

Gates: gofmt and vet clean, full nlp suite green (185s including the trained-model tests), mdlint reports no findings in the touched doc.

LANDED the GPT cache only, benchmark-validated on M2 Pro darwin/arm64 go1.26.5 via the existing bench-only kvAppendViaConcat flag (3 reps of -benchtime 5x, medians): BenchmarkGPTGenerate500 2,211,321,932 -> 159,364,963 B/op (13.9x less memory), 833 -> 630 ms (1.32x), allocs 310,777 -> 294,412. No benchmark covered GPT decode at all before this; the A/B pair was added beside the existing Llama one.

THE TIME PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND THE MEMORY ONE WAS RIGHT. The brief expected 2-3x wall clock by analogy to the Llama pair 2.59x; GPT measures 1.32x. A first 3-iteration run straddled 1.16-1.30x and was too noisy to report at all — 5 iterations were needed before three reps agreed within 1%. Anyone quoting this class of fix should lead with the memory figure, which is an order of magnitude and stable, not the wall clock.

THE BRIEF WAS PARTLY STALE: it claimed only LlamaCache had adopted appendKV. Cohere, Falcon, Gemma2 and DeepSeek-V2 had all adopted it since, so GPT, CLA and T5 were the actual remainder.

ALIASING AUDIT, done first as required, and recorded so it is not redone: no caller anywhere in nlp/ writes into a cache tensor in place, which is the only pattern that breaks under a view; retained views stay valid because appends only ever write row t and beyond; EvictStreaming replaces entries outright through GatherRows, which rowBuf.owns detects as a foreign view and resynchronizes from. Value identity was already pinned across F32/F64 by TestRowBufAppendMatchesConcatRows.

NOT DONE, and left as the remainder: nlp/cla.go (2 sites) and nlp/t5_decoder.go (2 sites). CLA is the one needing real care — it shares ONE cache slot across a group, keyed by g rather than l, and followers read cache.K[g] after the leader appends. nlp/streaming.go was DECLINED: it is already bounded to sinks+window, so it is O(window) not O(T), and its concat is nested inside keepSinkRecent, which would need eviction-aware truncation rather than a drop-in append.

GENERALIZED as perfscan PS2006 quadratic-cache-append with 5 fixtures and a mutation-probed detector. It finds exactly those 4 remaining sites and is silent on the fixed GPT path. Extending exprEqual to IndexExpr was required to prove a concat accumulates into its OWN slot; PS5001 shares that helper and stayed at 78 findings. Documented gap: the rule does not flag a concat nested inside another call, which is exactly the streaming shape.

ti: Build a synthetic T5Decoder so its KV cache can be benchmarked, then move it to the row buffer

note:
DONE, and the answer was MARGINAL. The blocker (a synthetic T5Decoder fixture) was built, the optimization was measured, and it did not pay off the way its siblings did: BenchmarkT5Decode500 15,908,982,321 -> 13,865,254,414 B/op (1.15x, 12.8% less) and 2,697 -> 2,679 ms (1.007x, no measurable time change), 3 reps of -benchtime 5x on M2 Pro darwin/arm64 go1.26.5. Compare GPT 13.9x and CLA 8.3x on the IDENTICAL transformation.

WHY, verified rather than inferred: relBiasRow calls RelBias.Bias(pos+1, pos+1) to build the FULL [pos+1, pos+1, heads] relative-position matrix on every token, copies one row out and discards the rest — O(T^2) allocation per token, O(T^3) over a decode. T5 spends 15.9 GB on the same 500 tokens / 4 layers / dim 256 where GPT spends 2.2 GB, so the KV cache was never its dominant cost. T-01KYJQ78FAFCG (compute the relative-position bias row directly) is the real T5 target, and the benchmark added here makes it measurable for the first time.

SHIPPED ANYWAY: 2 GB less per 500-token decode at no time cost, and it clears the last PS2006 findings — the check is clean tree-wide.

newTestT5Decoder is the reusable outcome: a small randomly-initialized decoder, because T5Decoder was previously constructible ONLY via T5DecoderFromHF from real safetensors. Deterministic but numerically meaningless — a shape and throughput fixture, NOT a parity fixture; value checks must keep using the transformers-anchored path. It carries its own smoke test, since a fixture that cannot complete a decode would make any benchmark on it measure nothing.

LEARNING CAST INTO internal/perfscan/PATTERNS.md under PS2006: a rule firing on a genuine quadratic shape does not imply a worthwhile win. The same fix returned 13.9x, 8.3x and 1.15x across three sites, decided purely by whether that shape dominated the site. Measure per site; never extrapolate from a sibling. crossK/crossV were deliberately left off the row buffer — the encoder is projected once, so they are never appended per token.

ti: Mamba2 prefill causal conv strides across row pointers — reorder to contiguous

note:
LANDED at 1.051x, and the PREDICTION IN THIS TASK WAS WRONG — recorded because the task stated it in advance. It predicted "closer to ExpertChoiceCombine 1.554x than to AQLM null" on the grounds that the access pattern was pathological rather than merely indirect. Measured interleaved (PROC-INTERLEAVE-001, 4 alternations, all arm spreads under 4%): BenchmarkMamba2Prefill_256 12,385,011 -> 11,783,600 ns and _512 23,302,900 -> 22,166,098 ns, both 1.051x, NEW winning all eight paired runs with non-overlapping ranges. The pathological access was real; the conv is simply a smaller share of prefill than assumed, since the SSM scan and the projections dominate. THE ENCLOSING-WORK HEURISTIC BEATS AN ACCESS-PATTERN ARGUMENT — that is now three-for-three (1.554x where the loop IS the work, 1.025x where it is a minority, ~1.00x where it is not the bottleneck, and 1.05x here).

Transform as specified: c/t/k reordered to t/k/c so both the output row and the source row walk contiguously; convW[c*K+k] becomes strided by K in exchange, cheap because convW is only D*K. Bit-identical by construction — for a fixed (t,c) the sum still runs over k ascending from convB[c].

GATE VERIFIED BEFORE BEING TRUSTED, as the task required: a single-ulp perturbation of one accumulation turns TestMamba2PrefillStateParity red, and so does reversing the k order. Do not assume a parity test covers a loop just because it is nearby.

BENCHMARKS WERE THE BLOCKER AND ARE NOW IN THE TREE: BenchmarkMamba2Prefill_{256,512}. Neither pre-existing Mamba prefill benchmark enters mixer2Prefill — both are Mamba1, verified by panic probe. The Mamba2 fixture also needs a tied Head; Prefill ends in a matmul against it, so a nil Head panics rather than erroring, which cost one debug cycle. Reuse benchMamba2Model for any further Mamba2 work.

SIBLINGS NOT DONE: the same loop shape exists in nlp/mamba2.go (the full-sequence Forward path) and nlp/quant_mamba2.go. At 1.05x propagation is worthwhile, but each needs its own benchmark and interleaved measurement — the share of total time differs per path and that is exactly what decides the result.

body:
Research swept the nlp incremental-decode paths. Four candidates, none yet benchmark-validated by the main agent; recorded so the measurement can be serialized.

1. jamba.go:209 JambaMoE.Forward evaluates every expert densely, including those top-k gave weight zero. Reached per token from jamba_decode.go:500. Fix mirrors nn.SparseMoE.ForwardDecode: mark used[i] in the existing top-k loop at 202-206 and skip unused experts at 209. Identical for every finite value (the removed addends were out_i times 0.0); diverges only on a negative-zero accumulator sign and on NaN/Inf out of an unselected expert, the same trade nn.SparseMoE already ships. Estimated 25 to 30 percent: these are GEMVs at arithmetic intensity about 0.125 MAC/byte, so weight bytes touched per step dominate, and MoE is 25.2 MB of a 42.5 MB step footprint; skipping 2 of 4 experts in each of 2 MoE layers removes 12.6 MB. Same defect at deepseekv2.go:400-402 and quant_jamba.go:199, neither covered by a benchmark.

2. jamba_decode.go:179-192 the S6 d loop in jambaMixerStep is serial over a free dimension and runs 8192 math.Exp per Mamba layer per token, 16384 per step at D=512 N=16. Parallelize over GOMAXPROCS with a work threshold. Bit-identical free-dimension jam: each d writes only its own H slice and y column and reads only its own inputs; backend/ref already parallelizes the same kernel. Estimated 20 to 30 percent, since arm64 has no assembly Exp and the pure-Go polynomial at 6 to 10 ns each is 115 to 165 microseconds against a step whose weight streaming alone is at least 210 microseconds.

3. jamba_decode.go:109,174-177,190,191 never got three fixes its mamba_decode.go twin already has: five rows2D(t)[0] calls that each allocate a header plus a full row copy and keep only row 0 (20 allocations and about 25 KB copied per step), an AtF64 dispatch on Dskip 1024 times per step, and SetF64 stores 1024 times per step. All three bit-identical, all three with a shipped in-repo precedent. Estimated 4 to 8 percent, mostly the allocations. Same rows2D pattern live at mamba_decode.go:135,190-193 and quant_mamba2.go:456.

4. t5_decoder.go:344-347 T5Decoder.Generate hand-rolls a vocab-length AtF64 loop per generated token instead of calling rowLogits from sample.go:1358. Bit-identical. NO benchmark covers Generate: benchT5Decode drives DecodeStep directly. Needs a new benchmark on the exported entry point before it can be sized.

BENCHMARK PROTOCOL NOTE that applies to all Jamba measurements: BenchmarkJambaDecode never resets its state, so appendKV grows the KV cache one row per iteration and attention cost is quadratic in b.N. A fixed -benchtime=200x is mandatory or A/B runs are not comparable.

REJECTED with reasons. simd.ExpScaledF64 is amd64-only under goexperiment.simd; on darwin/arm64 the portable body is element-by-element math.Exp, so porting it into Jamba is a no-op here. All 9 PS3010 four-partial-accumulator findings reassociate an inner reduction and every one sits under a doc comment claiming bit-identity with Forward or the ref kernel, so they are disqualified on correctness. mamba2_decode.go and quant_mamba2.go are already typed, vectorized and hoisted; what remains is about 9 scratch makes per layer per token, low single digit percent. falcon/gemma/cohere/stablelm/starcoder2 were tuned by T955-T958 and their benchmarks use tiny testdata models that measure dispatch overhead, not compute. t5_decoder.go:427 relBiasRow genuinely changes every step so it is not cacheable.

PS3025 TRIAGE from the same sweep: the 8 FMA findings in mamba_decode.go, jamba_decode.go and rwkv_decode.go are judged FALSE POSITIVES as they stand, because in each case the peer the doc names is also Go compiled for the same target with a structurally identical expression, so both sides contract or neither does. They would become real if a counterpart were ever a non-Go kernel pinned bit-exactly, or if one side gained a temporary that forces an intermediate rounding. Separately, PS3018 flags rwkv_decode.go:187 but MISSES the identical exp(0) pair at :184, where q is bound at 183 and reassigned at 186 — a real gap in that check.
